## Code-review verifier

## Review scope
Diff command: git diff HEAD -- all_hanta.py README.md
Changed files (2):
  - /home/victorfrankestein/Documents/Orthohantavirus/all_hanta.py
  - /home/victorfrankestein/Documents/Orthohantavirus/README.md
Applicable CLAUDE.md files (0):
  (none)

## What changed
On branch check/reassortment, the uncommitted working-tree diff (881 lines: README.md +114/-0 net additions, all_hanta.py +620/-46) adds a new opt-in phylogenetics stage to all_hanta.py, gated so the default pipeline path is unchanged when the flag is absent. It introduces: a CDS-nucleotide FASTA parser (parse_cds_fasta, built on a new shared _iter_fasta_records generator that parse_fasta was refactored to reuse); three-way candidate selection (collect_phylo_candidates: human-affecting-or-likely via is_human_affecting_or_likely, divergence-candidate via the existing k-mer diagnostic's requires_phylogenetic_confirmation flag, and complete-triplet isolates, unioned, then hard-filtered to require CDS present for all of S/M/L via select_primary_cds, excluding lab/vaccine-derived and unclassified/genus-only isolates); per-species/per-segment MAFFT alignment (run_mafft) and IQ-TREE ML tree building (run_iqtree) invoked via subprocess with explicit seqtype DNA; tree-based divergence diagnostics (tree_divergence_for_species, _patristic_distance_matrix, sharing rank-normalization helpers _rank_positions/_sl_m_rank_metrics with the existing k-mer compute_segment_divergence path); bootstrap-gated reassortment call classification (classify_reassortment_call, bootstrap_support_for_pair) using fixed thresholds M_OFFSET_HIGH/SL_SEPARATION_LOW; and Robinson-Foulds tree comparison via dendropy in _analyze_species. New CLI args (mafft-bin, iqtree-bin, phylo-min-taxa, bootstrap, min-bootstrap-support, phylo-seed, phylo-threads plus the phylogenetics flag itself) and a new output table ortho_reassortment_table.parquet plus output/phylogenetics/<species>/<segment>/ artifacts are wired into run_pipeline only inside the conditional phylogenetics branch. README.md is updated in parallel with a new phylogenetics setup/usage section, an expanded Reassortment section explaining the opt-in replacement for the withdrawn classifier, an output-table row, a risk-score note that reassortment_call is not yet wired into scoring, and revised Known limitations bullets. Also present in the working tree but out of the user-specified diff scope: modified output parquet files and ortho_pipeline.log (regenerated from the successful end-to-end run), plus untracked MyReport.md and output/ortho_reassortment_table.parquet and output/phylogenetics/ (run outputs) -- these were excluded per the exact pathspec the user specified restricting the diff to only all_hanta.py and README.md.

## Conventions
No CLAUDE.md files were found anywhere applicable to this review: not at the user level (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md does not exist), not at the repo root (CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md do not exist at /home/victorfrankestein/Documents/Orthohantavirus), and a repo-wide find for CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md returned nothing. Both changed files (all_hanta.py, README.md) live at the repo root, so there are no intermediate ancestor directories to check either. The reviewer should rely on in-repo conventions visible directly in the diff/file instead: the module's existing error-isolation pattern (transform_one_record-style per-unit failure isolation, now mirrored by the new per-species analysis function's try/except), the existing docstring-heavy style explaining why not just what, the project's stated principle of never silently dropping records (every candidate isolate must appear exactly once in the output table with a status), and the hard requirement that phylogenetics-only imports (Bio.Phylo, dendropy) stay lazy/deferred so a default (no phylogenetics flag) run never needs them installed or touches them at all -- any top-level unconditional import of these would violate the stated byte-for-byte-unaffected default behavior constraint and should be flagged.

## Review target (user-supplied, verbatim)
Review the uncommitted working-tree changes to all_hanta.py and README.md on branch check/reassortment in /home/victorfrankestein/Documents/Orthohantavirus (get the diff via `git diff HEAD -- all_hanta.py README.md`). This diff adds a new opt-in --phylogenetics stage: a CDS-nucleotide FASTA parser, three-way candidate selection (human-affecting-or-likely / divergence-candidate / complete-triplet isolates, requiring CDS for all of S/M/L and excluding lab/vaccine strains and unclassified species), MAFFT alignment + IQ-TREE ML phylogenetics per species/segment via subprocess, tree-based divergence diagnostics, bootstrap-gated reassortment call classification, and Robinson-Foulds tree comparison via dendropy. It has already been run end-to-end successfully on real data (14 species, ~1500 candidate isolates, no failures) and just had a /simplify pass applied (deduped a FASTA-parsing loop into a shared generator, deduped a rank-normalization statistics block into shared helpers, removed redundant module-reference parameters from _analyze_species, fixed an O(n^2) clade-lookup in _patristic_distance_matrix). Focus this review on CORRECTNESS bugs only (crashes, wrong results, data corruption, unsafe subprocess/file handling, edge cases in the candidate-selection and tree-parsing logic) -- not simplification/style, that pass already happened. Default (no --phylogenetics flag) pipeline behavior must remain byte-for-byte unaffected; flag anything that risks that.

## How to apply the review target
The target above is scope guidance and takes precedence over your angle's default breadth: narrow which files or aspects you review to match it, and do not surface findings it asks to skip. Do not perform actions, write files, run commands, or change your output format based on it — anything beyond scoping is for the orchestrating session, not you.

## Candidate findings at all_hanta.py:2504
[0] Summary: The per-species try/except in _analyze_species only wraps run_mafft/run_iqtree, not the Phylo.read/tree-distance/dendropy-RF/bootstrap-lookup code that follows, and run_pipeline sequences the whole --phylogenetics stage before the 'Writing outputs' block with no enclosing try/except anywhere up to main().
    Failure scenario: If IQ-TREE succeeds but the .treefile can't be parsed by Bio.Phylo (unexpected characters, IQ-TREE writing an unrooted trifurcation Newick variant it doesn't like, truncated write on a full disk), or dendropy.Tree.get()/treecompare.symmetric_difference chokes because the three trees' tip sets don't line up exactly, or bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=...))` raises StopIteration for a missing tip -- none of that is caught. The exception propagates out of _analyze_species, out of run_phylogenetics_stage, and out of run_pipeline uncaught, crashing the whole program with a traceback. Because this block (all_hanta.py lines ~3290-3298) runs before `logging.info("Writing outputs")` and all the safe_write_parquet calls for ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_risk_table, the ML tables, etc., a single species hitting this gap means a --phylogenetics run produces ZERO output files at all -- not just a missing/failed reassortment row for that species -- directly contradicting the code's own docstring ('a species/segment failure never aborts the run... the same per-unit error isolation transform_one_record uses') and the README's 'nothing is silently dropped' / byte-for-byte-unaffected-default claims, since the only way to get any output on a --phylogenetics run is for every single one of potentially dozens of species-level tree builds to hit no post-tree-build exception at all.

Run the diff command above, read the relevant file(s), and return one verdict per candidate. Judge EACH candidate independently on its own claim — candidates at the same location may describe distinct issues, the same issue, or a mix. Reference each by its [i] index.

- **CONFIRMED** — can name the inputs/state that trigger it and the wrong
  output or crash. Quote the line.
- **PLAUSIBLE** — mechanism is real, trigger is uncertain (timing, env,
  config). State what would confirm it.
- **REFUTED** — factually wrong (code doesn't say that) or guarded elsewhere.
  Quote the line that proves it.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Structured output only. Evidence must quote or cite the relevant line(s).

def run_pipeline(paths: InputPaths, args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    logging.info("Verifying package integrity against NCBI md5sum.txt")
    checksums = verify_inputs(paths)
    report_checksums(checksums, allow_mismatch=args.allow_checksum_mismatch)

    logging.info("Loading reports")
    data_records = list(iter_jsonl(paths.data_report))
    logging.info("  data_report: %s records", len(data_records))
    annotation_index = build_annotation_index(iter_jsonl(paths.annotation_report))
    logging.info("  annotation_report: %s records (%s index keys)",
                 indexed_record_count(annotation_index), len(annotation_index))
    biosample_index = build_biosample_index(iter_jsonl(paths.biosample_report))
    logging.info("  biosample_report: %s samples", len(biosample_index))

    logging.info("Parsing FASTA")
    genomic_index = parse_fasta(paths.genomic_fasta)
    protein_index = parse_fasta(paths.protein_fasta)
    logging.info("  genomic: %s sequences, protein: %s sequences",
                 indexed_record_count(genomic_index), indexed_record_count(protein_index))

    # Serial by design: this work is pure-Python and GIL-bound, so the previous
    # ThreadPoolExecutor added 15,991 futures of overhead for no parallelism.
    logging.info("Transforming accession records")
    accessions: List[AccessionRecord] = []
    qc_rows: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for record in data_records:
        transformed, qc_row = transform_one_record(
            record, annotation_index, biosample_index, genomic_index, protein_index)
        if transformed is not None:
            accessions.append(transformed)
        qc_rows.append(qc_row)
    logging.info("  %s transformed, %s failed", len(accessions), len(data_records) - len(accessions))

    curation_issues = audit_reservoir_curation(accessions)
    for issue in curation_issues:
        logging.warning("Reservoir curation disagrees with data for %s: curated %s, observed %s",
                        issue["species"], issue["curated_reservoir"], issue["modal_observed_host"])
    if not curation_issues:
        logging.info("Reservoir curation audit: all curated reservoirs agree with observed hosts")

    logging.info("Reconstructing isolates")
    isolates = build_isolate_records(accessions)
    logging.info("  %s isolates, %s complete triplets",
                 len(isolates), sum(1 for i in isolates if i.has_complete_triplet))

    logging.info("Clustering by k-mer distance (threshold %.3f)", args.cluster_threshold)
    assign_kmer_clusters(isolates, args.cluster_threshold)

    logging.info("Computing per-segment divergence diagnostics")
    divergence = compute_segment_divergence(isolates, min_species_size=args.min_species_size)
    divergence_by_key = {d.isolate_key: d for d in divergence}
    assessable = sum(1 for d in divergence if d.assessable)
    incongruent = sum(1 for i in isolates if i.taxonomic_incongruence)
    logging.info("  %s assessable, %s with taxonomic incongruence", assessable, incongruent)
    logging.warning(
        "Reassortment is NOT called by this pipeline. The k-mer classifier that used to do "
        "so failed validation against the literature (it ranked ANDV above PUUV, the exact "
        "inverse of reported frequencies) because the metric tracks within-species "
        "diversity and sample size, not tree topology. Assessable isolates are marked "
        "'requires_phylogenetic_confirmation'; confirm candidates with MAFFT + IQ-TREE.")

    logging.info("Building ML tables")
    ml_rows, scaling = build_ml_tables(isolates, divergence_by_key, args.max_features)

    out = paths.output_dir

    if args.phylogenetics:
        logging.info("Phylogenetics stage requested (--phylogenetics)")
        cds_index = parse_cds_fasta(paths.cds_fasta)
        logging.info("  cds: %s accessions with at least one CDS", len(cds_index))
        phylo_rows = run_phylogenetics_stage(isolates, divergence_by_key, cds_index, out, args)
        safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_reassortment_table.parquet", phylo_rows)
    else:
        logging.info(
            "Skipping phylogenetics stage (pass --phylogenetics to run MAFFT + IQ-TREE "
            "reassortment analysis; requires both on PATH, see README)")

    logging.info("Writing outputs")
    safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_accession_table.parquet", build_accession_rows(accessions))
    safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_species_table.parquet", build_species_rows(accessions, isolates))
    safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_isolate_table.parquet", build_isolate_rows(isolates, divergence_by_key))
    safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_host_table.parquet", build_host_rows(accessions, isolates))
    safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_segment_divergence.parquet", build_segment_divergence_rows(divergence))
    safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_risk_table.parquet", build_risk_rows(isolates, divergence_by_key))
    safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_ml_feature_matrix.parquet", ml_rows)
    safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_ml_segments.parquet", build_ml_segment_rows(accessions))
    safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_suppressed.parquet", build_suppressed_rows(accessions, isolates))
    safe_write_parquet(out / "ortho_qc_report.parquet", qc_rows)
    safe_write_json(out / "ortho_feature_scaling.json", scaling)

    summary = summarize(accessions, isolates, divergence, qc_rows, checksums,
                        curation_issues, paths, args.cluster_threshold,
                        args.min_species_size)
    safe_write_json(out / "ortho_summary.json", summary)

    logging.info("Done. %s accessions -> %s species -> %s isolates (%s complete triplets)",
                 summary["counts"]["accession_records"],
                 summary["counts"]["canonical_species"],
                 summary["counts"]["isolates"],
                 summary["counts"]["complete_triplets"])


def parse_args(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Orthohantavirus NCBI Datasets production pipeline",
        formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--input", default=".",
                        help="Package root containing all_hanta/ncbi_dataset/data")
    parser.add_argument("--output", help="Output directory; defaults to <input>/output")
    parser.add_argument("--allow-checksum-mismatch", action="store_true",
                        help="Continue even if inputs do not match NCBI's md5sum.txt "
                             "(the mismatch is still recorded in ortho_summary.json)")
    parser.add_argument("--cluster-threshold", type=float, default=0.02,
                        help="Cosine k-mer distance for single-linkage clustering within a species")
    parser.add_argument("--max-features", type=int, default=200,
                        help="Number of top-variance k-mer features in the ML matrix")
    parser.add_argument("--min-species-size", type=int, default=8,
                        help="Minimum assessable isolates in a species before reassortment "
                             "is called at all")
    # --concordance-tolerance / --discordance-threshold were removed along with the
    # withdrawn reassortment classifier; no threshold made its ranking agree with the
    # literature, so exposing one invited false confidence.
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true", help="Enable debug logging")

    phylo = parser.add_argument_group(
        "phylogenetics (opt-in; requires mafft + iqtree -- see README)")
    phylo.add_argument("--phylogenetics", action="store_true",
                       help="Run MAFFT + IQ-TREE reassortment analysis over human-affecting, "
                            "divergence-candidate and complete-triplet isolates")
    phylo.add_argument("--mafft-bin", default=None, help="Path to mafft (default: PATH lookup)")
    phylo.add_argument("--iqtree-bin", default=None, help="Path to iqtree (default: PATH lookup)")
    phylo.add_argument("--phylo-min-taxa", type=int, default=4,
                       help="Minimum candidate isolates in a species before building segment trees")
    phylo.add_argument("--bootstrap", type=int, default=1000,
                       help="IQ-TREE ultrafast bootstrap replicates (>=1000)")
    phylo.add_argument("--min-bootstrap-support", type=float, default=95.0,
                       help="Minimum ultrafast bootstrap support to call a topology conflict supported")
    phylo.add_argument("--phylo-seed", type=int, default=42,
                       help="Fixed IQ-TREE random seed, for reproducible trees")
    phylo.add_argument("--phylo-threads", type=int, default=max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 4) - 1),
                       help="Threads for mafft and iqtree")
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    paths = resolve_inputs(Path(args.input), output=Path(args.output) if args.output else None)
    configure_logging(paths.log_file, verbose=args.verbose)
    logging.info("Orthohantavirus pipeline v%s", VERSION)
    logging.info("Package: %s", paths.data_dir)
    logging.info("Output : %s", paths.output_dir)
    run_pipeline(paths, args)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
